clue.text: One having time to observe Foreign Office up front, taking stock of Boris's leadership

indicators.note: taking stock of here means taking on board, so the next piece joins on after the ministry's letters

parts.note: FO is the standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry

indicators.note: the leadership of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the name is used

parts.note: to observe something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A minister at the Foreign Office looks on while Boris Johnson, its former head, takes stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' just places the Foreign Office first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket timepiece on a chain is something that literally carries the time with it, a playful description.

clue.text: Avuncular cook, trousers tailored, lined

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets or takes in, so the cooking word wraps round the rest

parts.note: to fry is to cook

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so the letters of lined are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kindly uncle-like chef wears tailored, lined trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means kind and genial like an uncle, so warm and approachable.

clue.text: Hot in Gabon wearing Adam West's costume; it's skintight!

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the costume encloses the other letters

parts.note: Adam West played Batman on 1960s television, wearing the batsuit
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
G is the international vehicle code for Gabon

explanation.surface: Adam West sweats in his tight Batman suit in hot Gabon.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimwear clings closely to the body, so it is fairly described as tight against the skin.

clue.text: A soldier about after dark in Paris; he's getting a fixed income

indicators.note: after puts the insect soldier behind the French night

parts.note: an is a form of the indefinite article a
nuit is French for night
a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant

explanation.surface: A soldier hangs around Paris after nightfall, living on a fixed income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is just a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who receives a yearly payment, an annuity, draws a fixed income.

clue.text: He's chalked up extraordinary recent gains hedging Swedish celebs

extraordinary means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ABBA, the famous Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: Someone's extraordinary recent profits come from hedging bets on Swedish stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant is a huge naked figure cut into a chalk hillside in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill figure is outlined in white chalk on the slope, so he literally is chalked up there.

clue.text: Table support for web engineer

definitions.meaning: in snooker a long-legged rest that holds the cue over other balls is called by this name
an eight-legged creature that builds a web

explanation.surface: A table bracket is being sold as the work of a website developer.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker players call a raised cue rest by the arachnid's name, and the arachnid itself engineers webs.

clue.text: The first two appearances of Paddington Bear?

definitions.text: The first two appearances of Paddington Bear?

parts.words: The first two appearances of Paddington Bear?

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'first two appearances' as the first two letters of Paddington, P and A, and the bear appears.

clue.text: Desperate character of martial arts categorisation?

a grade of black-belt rank in judo or karate

clue.text: For 21 across, special flowers

explanation.surface: Special flowers are given in return for something.
explanation.definitionFit: These are among the best-known garden blooms, so they are an example of the class.

clue.text: In Germany, one way one from Ulm exhibits genius

parts.note: ein is German for one
ST is short for street, a way
Ulm is a German city, so one there is again ein

explanation.surface: A man from Ulm in Germany shows brilliance in one particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, so 'one from Ulm' doubles as a nod to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used as a byword for a brilliant mind.

clue.text: Complain to Nero, bored by bloke with monotonous voice

explanation.surface: Someone moans to the emperor Nero, who is bored by a dull droning man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks or chants in a level, unvarying tone is said to intone, so the speaker is one who does so.

clue.text: Knock pub sign off

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the word sign are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone knocks the sign off a pub wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' is cricket slang for a batter's turn at the crease, the period a cricketer spends batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter's knock is an informal word for their spell at the crease.

clue.text: Clamour for Tessa to get undressed, led by lust?

indicators.note: led by means the next piece comes after the earlier one in the answer

parts.note: lust read as NO. 1 SIN, i.e. the number one deadly sin

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle of the name

explanation.surface: Tessa is urged to strip, driven by desire, amid a lot of shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lust is cheekily read as 'No. 1 sin', spelt NO I SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamour is loud continuous noise, so the quality of being loud is a fair synonym.

clue.text: See 4

explanation.definitionFit: It is a herbal liqueur first made by monks at Fécamp in Normandy.

clue.text: Record independent archive, primarily of Christ's sayings

parts.note: a log is a record

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of archive is used

explanation.surface: An independent archive records, chiefly, the sayings of Jesus.

clue.text: Unconscious, go back dressed with surgical support

indicators.note: dressed with means wrapped in, so the bandage holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm

indicators.note: back means the word for urinating runs from right to left

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to pee

explanation.surface: A patient, knocked out, is sent back with a surgical brace on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEE into EEP, which goes inside SLING.

clue.text: County invites a politician to see coastal growth

parts.note: a shire is an English county

clue.text: They grow on trees in Spooner's brown flatlands

clue.text: General disorder as Bart, Homer Simpson initially held up

disorder means jumbled, so the letters of as and Bart are rearranged
up, in a down clue, means the pair of initials reads upwards
initially means the first letters of the two names

clue.text: Homo sapiens taking DNA test, having odd characters missing 4, 13, 21 down probably

parts.note: Homo sapiens is the human species

explanation.walkthrough: The chalk figure at Cerne Abbas in Dorset brandishes a huge club, so he is probably a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: The club-wielding chalk hill figure looks like a man out hunting, hence 'probably'.

clue.text: Tree pollarded, being thinner on top

clue.text: Turned out, turned out, the doctor's about

clue.text: See 4
Consequence of poor service for climbing/mountaineering equipment?

clue.text: Something to put in a pot; your cocoa, occasionally?
